# Pinned Python dependencies of the CLIENT-ONLY venv (scripts/setup_python.sh --client-only): an Apple silicon Mac that sends its audio to the
# company relay (remote ASR) and runs no local speech model (not verified on 8 GB Macs until they are measured).
# Install with:  pip install --no-deps -r requirements.client.txt      or, hash-locked,  scripts/make_hash_lock.sh  then
#                pip install --require-hashes --no-deps -r <the generated file>      (scripts/setup_python.sh --hash-lock FILE does this)
#
# Two packages, at exactly the versions of pipeline/requirements.lock.txt (scripts/test_scripts.sh pins that):
#   numpy       the audio code (WAV reading, VAD, echo cancellation, chunk planning) is numpy.
#   truststore  the operating system's trust store, used only for cloud-kind hosts (the relay is trusted through its pinned private CA with
#               the standard library alone; egress.py falls back to /etc/ssl/cert.pem when truststore is missing).
# Everything else of the full lock belongs to the local speech engine or is an HTTP client library: none of it is needed to talk to the
# relay through pipeline/mcap/egress.py (standard library http.client + ssl), and a smaller venv has a smaller supply chain: the in-process
# egress guard governs sockets that the pipeline opens, not the ones a bundled HTTP library could open (supply chain).
# A client-only venv cannot transcribe locally: ASR_ENGINE=whisper there ends in asr_policy_blocked, so pair it with a policy that allows the
# remote engine (docs/POLICY.md) or leave it to MDM groups that have the full runtime.
numpy==2.5.4
truststore==0.10.4
